newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest power eases with warmer weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest power eases with warmer weather.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. MidWest fell Monday with mild weather expected to dominate much of the region through to December 16, brokers and marketers said.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak non-firm power prices for Tuesday delivery were talked lower at $16.00-17.00 from $17.00-17.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) late last week, industry sources said.
"We saw the bottom drop out of SPP today, mostly because of the weather," said one SPP marketer, adding bids for peak hourly power reached as low as $14.00 Monday.
Also, Entergy's 1,173 megawatt Grand Gulf 1 nuclear power plant reached full power late last week following a shutdown for scheduled maintenance and refueling.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were said to be steady in the $13.00-15.00 area.
January/February peak SPP power was pegged lower at $24.75-25.25 from $26.10-27.25 late last week, the sources said.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power deals for Tuesday delivery were pegged lower at $19.00-20.00 from $22.00-24.00 for Monday delivery late last week.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power deals were pegged steady in the $12.00-14.00 range, the sources said.
In MAIN, peak, non-firm power for Tuesday delivery was pegged relatively steady at $19.50-22.00 from $19.50-21.50 late last week, the sources said.
MAIN off peak power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.
January/February MAIN peak power was said to be talked at $25.50-26.00 per MWh.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Tuesday were talked at $19.00-20.00 from $20.50-21.50 last week.
Off-peak, non-firm next-day ECAR power was notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00.
January and February peak ECAR prices were pegged steady at $23.75-24.25 per MWh.
